name: security-backup-restore-tenant-binding-review
intent: Backup/restore ownership across tenant and environment transitions
artifacts: Backup creation/access policy, restore target selection, encryption identity and restored application entitlements.
trace: Trace who can select a backup and where its contents become readable after restore, including tenant IDs retained or rewritten by the application.
experiment: Use isolated owned tenants and a synthetic backup; compare legitimate restore with an unauthorized source/target pairing.
disproof: An administrator-approved recovery is not tenant exposure; a backup identifier or restore job ID is not restored-data access.
repair: Bind backup source, requester and restored destination authority, verifying legitimate recovery and target isolation.
branch_decisions: Bind snapshot owner, environment, encryption identity and target tenant through restore and import. An authorized infrastructure operator may intentionally restore across environments; the issue is a restricted tenant selecting another tenant snapshot or receiving its data. Use tiny local backup fixtures and keep privileged snapshot creation separate from attacker-controlled restore selection.
operational_method: Retain the restore mapping for tenant/principal IDs, ownership, encryption identity and environment-specific credentials/capabilities. Inspect the pre-open gate that applies new mappings, revocations and publication policy before restored data becomes available. Compare a synthetic restore into its rightful tenant with a changed target principal/environment; a backup authorized for an infrastructure operator is not automatically authorized for an application tenant.
